name: Japanese Violet
lede: Japanese Violet is a dark reddish-purple named for the sumire, the wild violet flower that gives it its Japanese name.

sections.title: In Japan: Sumire-iro
sections.body:
The name is written 菫色, romanized Sumire-iro, which our color library glosses as "violet color" [1]. *Sumire* is the Japanese word for violet, the small spring-flowering plant of the genus *Viola*, and the color is named for it the same way the English word violet is [1]. Our sources do not give a date for when the name was first fixed to this exact shade [1].

The nearest named neighbor by measured color is [[auricula-purple]], duller than this shade; [[dark-byzantium]] sits close by, also duller [2]. [[light-aubergine]] and [[grape]] sit a little further out [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for Japanese Violet in 9 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.04 percent, rarer than 77 percent of the named colors we track, as photographed [3]. The earliest archive match is dated 1853, in a work attributed to Eduardo Cano; the latest is 1915, across 4 dated paintings [3]. The archive's early centuries are thin, so that first date is a floor, not a first [3]. Deep reddish-purples like this one are uncommon across our whole archive, so a handful of paintings is not unusual for this family of colors [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications [3].
